findings.title: Federated recovery-code credential cannot be removed via removeStoredCredentialById
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. When all its codes are used, the authenticator calls `credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(id)`, which only works on credentials stored in the Keycloak DB.

For a federated credential this call does nothing. It also may receive a null or foreign id: the test provider's `createFromValues` model never sets an id. The exhausted credential therefore stays in user storage.

As a result, `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true and the user keeps being sent to the recovery-code form with no usable codes. The federated case needs its own handling, for example `disableCredentialType` or an update through the user storage.

findings.title: Federated providers must expose recovery codes in Keycloak's internal JSON format or login breaks
findings.body:
`getCredential` prefers `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`. Callers such as `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (`.get()` without a check) and the authenticator then pass the result to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel`, which parses the credentialData as Keycloak's internal hashed-codes JSON.

A user storage provider can accept recovery codes through `updateCredential` and report `isConfiguredFor` true without returning a compatible model from `getCredentials`. In that case login throws `NoSuchElementException` or a parse error and fails with a 500.

This new contract for user storage providers is implicit and undocumented. The code should handle a missing or malformed credential gracefully, or the contract should be documented.

findings.title: Test provider never consumes codes; test does not cover code consumption
findings.body:
The provider's `isValid` accepts any stored code, regardless of which code number was requested, and never marks a code as used.

As a result, `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode` always returns the same code, and the exhausted-codes path in the authenticator is never reached. The new test only logs in once.

Code consumption and the all-codes-used flow for federated credentials are left untested. That flow is broken (see the `removeStoredCredentialById` finding).

findings.title: getCredentials NPE when user not in map
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null. Other methods in this provider guard against that (`if (myUser == null) return false`), but `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` directly. It throws a NullPointerException for users not present in the in-memory map.
